text:
**Short answer: a ~1,000 Wh power station is enough for one night. I'd pick the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 (1,024 Wh) or the BLUETTI AC180 (1,152 Wh).**

**Why 1,000 Wh works**
- The Department of Energy lists typical electric blankets at about 60 W (single) and 100 W (double). Sunbeam rates its full-size heated blankets at 110 W. At 100 W, a 1,024 Wh station runs a blanket for about 8 hours, according to [Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/24/power-station-electric-blanket/).
- [Blackoutwise](https://www.blackoutwise.com/will-it-run/electric-blanket) says a queen blanket is rated about 150 W but cycles to an average near 75 W. On that basis, a 1,000 Wh station lasts about 11–12 hours.
- The sources disagree on how much power a blanket draws. One site assumes about 260 W for a queen blanket, which would need roughly 2,600 Wh for 8 hours ([HomePowerFacts](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/electric-blanket/)). The DOE and Sunbeam figures are much lower, so I'd trust 100–150 W. Check the wattage on your blanket's label.

**My picks**
1. **BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 (1,024 Wh, about $380–$500, 25 lb).** It's [Blackoutwise's top pick](https://www.blackoutwise.com/best/best-power-station-for-electric-blanket). They say it runs a 150 W blanket for about 12 hours, which covers a full 8-hour night with some left over.
2. **BLUETTI AC180 (1,152 Wh, $449).** [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-heated-blanket-all-night) says it can run one 120 V blanket all night, or two on low. It uses about 15 W of its own power with AC on. Dealectric also says it's due back in stock in late November, so it may not be available right now. [Buy at Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180).
3. **EcoFlow Delta 3 Classic (1,024 Wh).** [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/pro/this-ecoflow-delta-3-classic-bundle-is-the-home-backup-battery-id-keep-ready-for-winter-storms-and-its-usd119-off-at-best-buy) lists the bundle with a 45W solar panel at $479 (was $598) at Best Buy. It has an LFP battery rated for 3,000 cycles, 1,800 W output, and a five-year warranty. TechRadar hasn't tested this model, and the 45W panel is too small to recharge it quickly.

**Two nights, or a bigger load:** [Blackoutwise](https://www.blackoutwise.com/best/best-power-station-for-electric-blanket) says the Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 runs a 150 W blanket for about 23 hours.

**Avoid:**
- **Units around 300 Wh.** A 286–288 Wh unit runs a 150 W blanket for only about 3–3.5 hours, and the 499 Wh Yeti 500 for about 5.5 hours ([Blackoutwise](https://www.blackoutwise.com/best/best-power-station-for-electric-blanket)).
- **Small inverters.** The 300 Wh Tenergy T320 has a 200 W inverter and can't run a 120 V queen blanket on high ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-heated-blanket-all-night)).

**Tips**
- Plug the blanket straight into the station. Sunbeam's manuals say not to use extension cords or power strips ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-heated-blanket-all-night)).
- Keep the station off the bed and away from the blanket's folds.
- If you want warmth from the same battery, a blanket is far more efficient than a space heater. A 1,500 W heater would drain a 1 kWh unit in about 35 minutes ([Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/24/power-station-electric-blanket/)).
